instruction: Center-align the content text and change the title font color to green.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully changed content font size to 12, font color to orange, and slide background to red in LibreOffice Impress. Completed in 40 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select text in Impress, change font properties (size, color, bold, italic), change slide background color via properties panel.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests text alignment change and a different font color (green). Alignment is a related but different formatting operation from the original font size/color task.
metadata.explanation: Getter reads content paragraph alignment and title font color from saved pptx. Metric gives 0.5 for center alignment and 0.5 for green title color.

llm_judge_reasons: Both instruction requirements (center-align content, green title color) are verified with appropriate partial credit (0.5 each)
Getter correctly extracts content alignment from paragraph properties and title color from font.color.rgb using python-pptx
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' - directly accesses expected.get('content_alignment') and expected.get('title_color')
Substring match for alignment handles python-pptx enum string representation (e.g. 'CENTER (1)' contains 'CENTER')
Color comparison allows reasonable green variants (00FF00, 008000, 00B050, 00B000) for the 'green' instruction
Postconfig correctly saves the file with Ctrl+S before getter reads it
Minor: getter only checks first paragraph alignment and first run color - adequate for typical slides but could miss multi-paragraph/multi-run cases
Minor: shape indexing (shapes[0]=title, shapes[1]=content) is standard for title+content layouts but is a fragile assumption
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using slide.placeholders with placeholder type checks (TITLE, BODY) instead of shapes[0]/shapes[1] for more robust shape identification
Consider checking alignment across all content paragraphs, not just the first one
